chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Abd al-Rahman Abdullah ibn Sa'dan ibn Sahl al-Yashkuri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Yazid (meaning Ibn Zari'a) narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samurah, saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This religion will remain mighty and strong, and they will be victorious over those who oppose them, until there are twelve Caliphs.' Then the Prophet said a word that the people could not hear. I asked my father: 'What was the word that the people could not hear?' He said: 'He said: They are all from Quraysh.'

key_terms.أَصْمَنَهَا: They could not hear it clearly

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Caliphs mentioned in the hadith and what is their lineage?
ai.summary: This narration from Jabir ibn Samurah, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of the Twelve Imams as divinely appointed successors from the Quraysh, specifically the Banu Hashim. The phrase 'all of them from Quraysh' underscores their tribal legitimacy and continuity with the Prophet’s lineage, while the promise that the religion remains 'mighty and strong' until their appearance highlights the eschatological significance of their leadership in preserving the faith against opposition.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Abu Abdul Rahman Abdullah ibn Sa’edan ibn Sahl al-Yashkari quoted Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam, on the authority of Yazid - ibn Zari’a, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “This dear and invulnerable religion will not end and it shall overcome all its enemies until there come twelve Caliphs.” Then the Prophet (MGB) said something which the people could not hear. I asked my father, ‘What was it that the people could not hear?’ My father said, ‘The Prophet (MGB) said, ‘They are all from the Quraysh.’”
